queen_checkmate.name: Queen Checkmate
queen_checkmate.description: Learn to checkmate with King and Queen against a lone King.
key_concepts: Use the Queen to restrict the enemy King
Push the enemy King to the edge of the board
Bring your King closer to help
Avoid stalemate!

explanations.0: Start by checking the King to push it back.
explanations.2: Bring your King into the action - it needs to help!
explanations.4: Keep restricting the enemy King's squares.
explanations.12: The enemy King is running out of space.
explanations.20: Checkmate! The King is trapped on the edge.

common_mistakes: Don't stalemate! Always leave the enemy King a square (until checkmate)
Don't rush - bring your King to help
Use checks strategically, not randomly

rook_checkmate.name: Rook Checkmate
rook_checkmate.description: Learn to checkmate with King and Rook against a lone King.
key_concepts: Cut off the enemy King with the Rook
Use your King to push the enemy King back
The 'box' technique - shrink the enemy King's space
Opposition is key!

explanations.0: Check to push the King back and cut it off.
explanations.2: Now bring your King into the fight!
explanations.8: The 'box' is getting smaller - enemy King has less space.
explanations.20: Opposition! Your King faces the enemy King.
explanations.29: Checkmate! Rook delivers the final blow.

common_mistakes: The Rook alone can't checkmate - your King must help
Don't give pointless checks - improve your King's position
Watch out for stalemate in the corner

opposition.name: The Opposition
opposition.description: Master the key concept of Opposition in King and Pawn endgames.
key_concepts: Opposition: Kings face each other with one square between
The side NOT to move has the opposition (advantage)
Use opposition to force the enemy King aside
Critical for promoting pawns

explanations.0: First, we need to get our King in front of the pawn.
explanations.2: Push the pawn to gain space.
explanations.6: We have the opposition! Enemy King must move aside.
explanations.14: Key position - our King is in front of the pawn.
explanations.24: With opposition, the pawn will promote!

common_mistakes: Don't push the pawn too early - King goes first!
Losing the opposition often means a draw
Always get your king in front of the pawn — that’s the key idea.

rule_of_square.name: Rule of the Square
rule_of_square.description: Learn when your King can catch a passed pawn.
key_concepts: Draw a square from the pawn to the promotion square
If your king can step into the square, it catches the pawn.
Count carefully - one wrong square loses!
Diagonal moves are just as fast as straight moves

explanations.0: The pawn is on b6. Draw a square b6-b1-g1-g6. Can our King enter?
explanations.2: We're inside the square! We can catch the pawn.
explanations.9: We caught it! The King reaches the pawn in time.

common_mistakes: The square is drawn from the pawn, not the king.
Count the squares carefully before deciding to chase
Remember: King moves diagonally just as fast!

lucena_position.name: Lucena Position (Building a Bridge)
lucena_position.description: The most important rook endgame technique - the Bridge.
key_concepts: Rook + Pawn vs Rook is often won with the Lucena technique
The King hides behind the pawn from checks
Build a 'bridge' with your Rook to block enemy checks
This wins 95% of Rook + Pawn vs Rook positions

explanations.0: First, move the Rook to the 4th rank to prepare the bridge.
explanations.2: Now step out with the King.
explanations.4: Black checks, but we keep moving the King down.
explanations.10: The Bridge! Rook blocks the check, pawn will promote.

common_mistakes: Don't try to promote immediately - build the bridge first
The Rook on the 4th rank is key to blocking checks
Be patient - this technique always works

philidor_position.name: Philidor Position (The Drawing Technique)
philidor_position.description: Learn how to draw Rook + Pawn vs Rook from the defending side.
key_concepts: Keep your Rook on the 6th rank (3rd rank for Black)
This prevents the enemy King from advancing
When the pawn advances to the 6th, go to the back rank
Check from behind - infinite checks draw!

explanations.0: Black's King stays in front of the pawn.
explanations.4: Rook to the 6th rank - the key defensive position!
explanations.7: When the pawn advances, Rook goes to the back rank.
explanations.10: Now we check from behind - White can't escape!

common_mistakes: Don't let your King get pushed to the side
Keep the Rook on the 6th until the pawn moves there
From behind, you have infinite checking distance

stalemate_trap.name: Stalemate: Leave Them One Square
stalemate_trap.description: Learn how to finish a won game without letting it slip to a draw.
key_concepts: Stalemate is a draw. It happens when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check.
Before you move, ask one question: after this, can they still move?
When you are far ahead, leave the enemy king one square until you are ready to mate.
A queen takes squares away fast. That is why it wins games and why it draws them.

explanations.0: Their king is on a4 with one square left: a3. Qb4 is mate. Two other moves here end the game as a draw instead: Kc3 and g4 both take a3 away while the king is not in check.

common_mistakes: Taking the last square away without giving check. That is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
Moving the king closer when the enemy king is already short of squares.
Pushing a pawn 'to be safe' when it covers the one square they had left.
